name: Mutual Non-Disclosure Agreement
description: Lets two parties share confidential information with each other for a stated purpose while each keeps the other's information private.

name: Cloud Service Agreement
description: Terms for a provider selling cloud software or SaaS to a customer, covering access, fees, data, warranties and liability.

fields.label: Cloud Service
fields.ask: What cloud service or product is the customer subscribing to?

fields.label: Order Date
fields.ask: When does the order start?

fields.label: Subscription Period
fields.ask: How long is each subscription period (1 year is common)?

fields.label: Non-Renewal Notice Date
fields.ask: The subscription renews automatically unless a party gives notice: how many days before the end of a period must that notice come?
fields.default: 30 days before the end of the Subscription Period

fields.label: Fees
fields.ask: What are the fees, and how often are they charged?

fields.label: Payment Process
fields.ask: How will the customer pay: by invoice, with how many days to pay, or by automatic payment (invoicing annually in advance, due in 30 days, is common)?

fields.label: Technical Support
fields.ask: What technical support will the provider give?
fields.default: email support during the provider's business hours

fields.label: Effective Date
fields.ask: When should the agreement take effect?

fields.label: Governing Law
fields.ask: Which state's or country's law should govern the agreement?

fields.label: Chosen Courts
fields.ask: Which courts should handle disputes (usually the state or federal courts in one city in the governing law's state)?

fields.label: General Cap Amount
fields.ask: What is the general limit on each party's liability?
fields.default: 1 times the fees paid or payable in the 12 months before the claim

fields.label: Provider Covered Claims
fields.ask: Which third-party claims will the provider defend the customer against?
fields.default: any claim that the Cloud Service infringes or misappropriates a third party's intellectual property rights

fields.label: Customer Covered Claims
fields.ask: Which third-party claims will the customer defend the provider against?
fields.default: any claim that Customer Content, or the customer's use of the Cloud Service in breach of the Agreement, infringes a third party's rights or violates the law

fields.label: DPA
fields.ask: Is there a Data Processing Agreement between the parties? If so, which one?

fields.label: Changes to the Standard Terms
fields.ask: Would you like any changes to the standard terms (most people have none)?

name: Service Level Agreement
description: Uptime and support commitments, with service credits, for a cloud service. Used alongside a Cloud Service Agreement.

fields.label: Agreement
fields.ask: Which main agreement does this Service Level Agreement attach to (its name, the parties and its date)?

fields.label: Target Uptime
fields.ask: What monthly uptime should the provider aim for (99.9% is common)?

fields.label: Uptime Credit
fields.ask: What credit does the customer get when uptime falls below the target?
fields.default: 10% of the monthly fee if uptime is below the Target Uptime

fields.label: Scheduled Downtime
fields.ask: When may the provider take the service down for planned maintenance?
fields.default: with at least 48 hours' notice, outside the customer's business hours

fields.label: Target Response Time
fields.ask: How quickly should the provider respond to support requests (1 business day is common)?

fields.label: Response Time Credit
fields.ask: What credit does the customer get for each missed response time?
fields.default: 5% of the monthly fee per missed response

fields.label: Support Channel
fields.ask: How should the customer contact support (e.g. an email address or ticket system)?

fields.label: Changes to the Standard Terms
fields.ask: Would you like any changes to the standard terms (most people have none)?

name: Data Processing Agreement
description: How a provider processes personal data on a customer's behalf under privacy laws such as GDPR. Used alongside a Cloud Service Agreement.

fields.label: Agreement
fields.ask: Which main agreement does this Data Processing Agreement attach to (its name, the parties and its date)?

fields.label: Categories of Data Subjects
fields.ask: Whose personal data will be processed (usually the customer's end users and employees)?

fields.label: Categories of Personal Data
fields.ask: What kinds of personal data will be processed (usually names, contact details and usage data)?

fields.label: Special Category Data
fields.ask: Will any special category data, such as health, biometric or religious data, be processed (most agreements have none)?

fields.label: Special Category Data Restrictions or Safeguards
fields.ask: (Only if special category data is processed.) What extra restrictions or safeguards apply to it?

fields.label: Frequency of Transfer
fields.ask: How often will personal data be transferred to the provider?

fields.label: Nature and Purpose of Processing
fields.ask: What will the provider do with the personal data, and why?
fields.default: receiving, holding, using and protecting the data to provide the services under the Agreement

fields.label: Duration of Processing
fields.ask: How long will the processing last?
fields.default: for the term of the Agreement, plus the time needed to return or delete the data

fields.label: Approved Subprocessors
fields.ask: Which subprocessors may the provider use (a list, or a web page that lists them)?

fields.label: Security Policy
fields.ask: Which security policy will the provider follow?

fields.label: Provider Security Contact
fields.ask: Who should the customer contact about security issues (an email address)?

fields.label: Governing Member State
fields.ask: If personal data is transferred out of the EEA or UK, which country's law governs the transfer clauses?
fields.default: Ireland for EEA transfers; England and Wales for UK transfers

fields.label: Changes to the Standard Terms
fields.ask: Would you like any changes to the standard terms (most people have none)?

name: Professional Services Agreement
description: Terms for a provider performing services for a customer under statements of work, covering deliverables, fees and ownership.

fields.label: Services
fields.ask: What services will the provider perform?

fields.label: Deliverables
fields.ask: What will the provider deliver, if anything (some services have no deliverables)?

fields.label: Time of Assignment
fields.ask: (Only if there are deliverables.) When does ownership of deliverables pass to the customer: when created, or once paid for?

fields.label: Rejection Period
fields.ask: (Only if there are deliverables.) How long does the customer have to review and reject a deliverable?

fields.label: Resubmission Period
fields.ask: (Only if there are deliverables.) How long does the provider have to fix and resubmit a rejected deliverable?

fields.label: Fees
fields.ask: What are the fees for the services (e.g. a fixed price or an hourly rate)?

fields.label: Payment Period
fields.ask: How long does the customer have to pay each invoice?
fields.default: 30 days from receipt of the invoice

fields.label: SOW Term
fields.ask: How long will the services run?

fields.label: Customer Obligations
fields.ask: What must the customer do or provide (e.g. access, information, staff)?

fields.label: Effective Date
fields.ask: When should the agreement take effect?

fields.label: Governing Law
fields.ask: Which state's or country's law should govern the agreement?

fields.label: Chosen Courts
fields.ask: Which courts should handle disputes (usually the state or federal courts in one city in the governing law's state)?

fields.label: General Cap Amount
fields.ask: What is the general limit on each party's liability?
fields.default: 1 times the fees paid or payable in the 12 months before the claim

fields.label: Increased Claims
fields.ask: Should any kinds of claims (e.g. breach of confidentiality or data protection) have a higher liability limit?

fields.label: Increased Cap Amount
fields.ask: (Only if there are Increased Claims.) What is the higher liability limit for them?

fields.label: Unlimited Claims
fields.ask: Should any kinds of claims have no liability limit at all?

fields.label: Provider Covered Claims
fields.ask: Which third-party claims will the provider defend the customer against?
fields.default: any claim that the Deliverables infringe or misappropriate a third party's intellectual property rights

fields.label: Customer Covered Claims
fields.ask: Which third-party claims will the customer defend the provider against?
fields.default: any claim that materials the customer provides infringe a third party's rights

fields.label: Additional Warranties
fields.ask: Does either party give any warranties beyond the standard terms?

fields.label: Insurance Minimums
fields.ask: What insurance must the provider carry, if any?

fields.label: DPA
fields.ask: Is there a Data Processing Agreement between the parties? If so, which one?

fields.label: Security Policy
fields.ask: Which security policy will the provider follow, if any?

fields.label: Customer Policies
fields.ask: Which customer policies must the provider follow, if any?

fields.label: Changes to the Standard Terms
fields.ask: Would you like any changes to the standard terms (most people have none)?

fields.label: Warranty Period

fields.label: Deletion Procedure
fields.ask: When the license ends, how must the customer remove the software?
fields.default: uninstall the Software, delete all copies and confirm this in writing

fields.label: Effective Date

fields.label: Governing Law

fields.label: Customer Covered Claims
fields.ask: Which third-party claims will the customer defend the provider against?

fields.label: Additional Warranties

fields.label: Changes to the Standard Terms
